speaker_role: founder/counselor at a college counseling company (ElevatEd School); claims to have read Stanford essays from students
commercial_incentive: Channel promotes its own paid counseling/essay services; brief pitch to subscribe and request content.
key_insights: Stanford-specific essays should name concrete programs, majors and institutes; the speaker says nearly none of the essays he reviewed did so.
Explain which academic opportunities attract you and how you would contribute to them, not only benefit from them.
For the roommate prompt, avoid bragging or diary-style rambling; choose two or three personal quirks and tie each to something you could do with a roommate.
Write the roommate essay in a friendly conversational voice to convey personality and dorm fit.
Speaker claims Stanford values people who already executed on ideas and made an impact, so show evidence of doing rather than only stating a vision.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker says Stanford has three undergrad schools, more than 65 majors and 15 research institutes.
Anecdote: an international student admitted after spending a summer planting 5,000 trees (speaker's claim).
notable_or_distinctive: Worked roommate-essay example using a fictional Spider-Man persona to show picking 2-3 traits and linking to shared activities.
reliability_notes: Speaker's inferences about what Stanford wants are opinion; program counts and mission-statement reading are unverified; auto-captions slightly garbled; headline claim that getting in is easy is hype.
